headline: High: next-ai-draw-io can ingest and send content via MCP/broad egress, while LlamaFactory lacks isolation and may be exposed through shared workflows.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: next-ai-draw-io uses MCP and natural-language commands, so attacker-controlled document content can plausibly steer its prompts; LlamaFactory has no shared channel or parser surface documented, so the pairwise bridge is indirect. Uncertainty is limited by docs-only evidence, so medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF next-ai-draw-io ingests untrusted document text through MCP or browser workflows, prompt injection is possible.
IF LlamaFactory is manually fed outputs from next-ai-draw-io, those outputs can be treated as instructions.
mitigations: Restrict next-ai-draw-io to trusted documents only.
Add a human review step before copying any generated text into LlamaFactory.
Disable MCP access for untrusted sessions.
Use separate workspaces for the two agents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: next-ai-draw-io has broad network egress, multiple third-party API targets, and handles API keys; LlamaFactory is a local open-source agent with no egress, but the pair still creates a default leakage path if shared documents or prompts contain secrets. Because one agent can transmit content externally, the safer severity is high.
conditions: IF sensitive files are opened in next-ai-draw-io, their contents can be sent to external model APIs.
IF API keys or secrets are present in shared prompts, next-ai-draw-io may expose them over network egress.
mitigations: Do not load secrets into next-ai-draw-io.
Use a redaction pass before any document upload.
Route next-ai-draw-io to a local-only model backend.
Separate credentials from the workspace.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on outbound prompts.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LlamaFactory cannot write files, modify git, or use network egress, so it has little direct conflict surface. next-ai-draw-io can support multiple instances and uses files/MCP, but the profiles do not show overlapping write access to the same mutable resource. The interaction is therefore limited and mostly avoidable.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable workspace, file-level contention can occur.
IF next-ai-draw-io writes diagram files while another process edits them, conflicts may appear.
mitigations: Assign separate directories to each agent.
Avoid concurrent edits to the same diagram file.
Use file locking if shared storage is unavoidable.
Keep LlamaFactory read-only in shared workflows.
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking.

D_cascading_error.rationale: next-ai-draw-io is designed for natural-language, AI-assisted visualization and can output diagrams or text that a downstream operator may trust; LlamaFactory can generate model outputs but has no documented verification layer. The pair creates a plausible chain where one agent's output becomes the other's input without validation, so medium is warranted.
conditions: IF outputs from next-ai-draw-io are copied into LlamaFactory as authoritative text, errors can cascade.
IF LlamaFactory is used to summarize or transform unverified diagram content, mistakes can propagate.
mitigations: Require manual verification before reuse of generated content.
Annotate outputs as untrusted drafts.
Use a checklist for factual claims in diagrams.
Keep source documents attached to downstream reviews.
requires-engineering: add validation against original inputs.

E_compliance.rationale: next-ai-draw-io handles files and sends requests to multiple external AI providers, while LlamaFactory is open-source and local-only. The pair can therefore create a retention/residency mismatch when the same documents are processed through both systems, especially if regulated content is uploaded to the networked agent. No direct residency certification is documented, so uncertainty pushes to medium.
conditions: IF regulated documents are processed in next-ai-draw-io, they may leave the local environment.
IF the same data is later handled by LlamaFactory under different retention rules, policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Keep regulated data out of next-ai-draw-io.
Use a local-only backend for sensitive workflows.
Document retention rules for both agents.
Separate compliant and non-compliant datasets.
requires-engineering: add residency-aware routing.
